title: What Happens When You Cry?
description:
Tears are made by glands behind the upper outside corner of each eye. Every blink drains used tears into your tear ducts, which empty into the back of your nose. When you cry, tears flow in faster than usual and drain into your throat, which is why you might feel stuffy after crying. Emotional tears, triggered by feelings like sadness or joy, contain more stress hormones and natural painkillers than everyday tears.
